title: Past narration
matching: Typed answers ignore letter case, extra spaces, apostrophe style and final . ! or ? punctuation. Accents and every other character count. Multiple-choice answers must match exactly.

lessons.title: Irregular pretérito perfeito: ser/ir, fazer, dar, ter, vir, pôr, dizer, trazer, poder, saber, querer, ver
lessons.explanation: Use the pretérito perfeito for a completed event. Many frequent verbs change their stem and have no regular endings in the eu and você/ele forms. Ser and ir share one form: fui, foi, fomos, foram. Learn the stems: fiz/fez (fazer), dei/deu (dar), tive/teve (ter), vim/veio (vir), pus/pôs (pôr), disse (dizer), trouxe (trazer), pude/pôde (poder), soube (saber), quis (querer), vi/viu (ver). Poder and pôr take a circumflex in the ele form (pôde, pôs). Do not add regular endings to the old stem: say fiz, not fazi.

examples.pt: Ontem eu fui ao médico e ele me disse que estou bem.
examples.en: Yesterday I went to the doctor and he told me I am well.

examples.pt: Elas vieram cedo e trouxeram o bolo.
examples.en: They came early and brought the cake.

examples.pt: Nós não pudemos ver o jogo, mas soubemos o resultado.
examples.en: We could not watch the game, but we found out the result.

lessons.title: Pretérito imperfeito: habits, descriptions and the irregular verbs
lessons.explanation: Use the pretérito imperfeito for habits, descriptions and actions in progress in the past, without saying when they started or ended. Regular endings: -ar verbs take -ava, -avas, -ava, -ávamos, -avam (falava); -er and -ir verbs take -ia, -ias, -ia, -íamos, -iam (comia). The nós form is always accented: falávamos, comíamos, tínhamos. Only four verbs are irregular: ser (era, éramos, eram), ter (tinha, tínhamos), vir (vinha, vínhamos) and pôr (punha, púnhamos). Ir is regular: ia, íamos. The imperfect also makes a request or wish sound polite: eu queria um café.

examples.en: When I was a child, we lived near the sea.

examples.pt: Meu avô sempre tinha tempo para brincar conosco.

lessons.title: Perfeito or imperfeito in a short narrative
lessons.explanation: In a story, use the imperfeito for the background: the weather, what people were doing, how things were, and habits. Use the perfeito for the events that move the story forward, one after another, or that interrupt the background. Compare: Eu dormia quando o telefone tocou (background, then an interruption). Words that often go with the imperfeito are sempre, todos os dias, enquanto and naquela época. Words that often go with the perfeito are de repente, ontem, então and uma vez. Choose by meaning, not by the word: the same verb can take either form.

examples.pt: Chovia muito quando eu saí de casa.
examples.en: It was raining a lot when I left home.

examples.pt: Enquanto ela cozinhava, eu arrumei a sala.
examples.en: While she cooked, I tidied the living room.

examples.pt: De repente, o cachorro latiu e todos acordaram.
examples.en: Suddenly the dog barked and everyone woke up.

lessons.title: Past participles: regular, irregular and double forms
lessons.explanation: Regular participles end in -ado for -ar verbs (falado) and -ido for -er and -ir verbs (comido, partido). Learn the frequent irregular ones: feito (fazer), dito (dizer), escrito (escrever), aberto (abrir), visto (ver), posto (pôr), coberto (cobrir), vindo (vir). Used as an adjective or in the passive, the participle agrees with the noun: a porta aberta, as cartas escritas. A few verbs have two participles: the regular one goes with ter or haver (tinha pagado), and the short one goes with ser and estar (foi pago, está aceito). In everyday Brazilian speech, the short form is often used with ter as well.

examples.pt: O trabalho já está feito e a porta está aberta.
examples.en: The work is already done and the door is open.

examples.pt: Os documentos foram escritos em português.

lessons.title: Mais-que-perfeito composto: tinha + participle
lessons.explanation: Use the mais-que-perfeito composto for an event that had already happened before another past moment. Form it with the imperfeito of ter (tinha, tinhas, tinha, tínhamos, tinham) plus the participle: eu tinha saído, nós tínhamos feito. The participle does not change. It often appears with já (already), ainda não (not yet), nunca (never) and antes (before). Compare: Quando cheguei, ela saiu (she left after I arrived) and Quando cheguei, ela já tinha saído (she was already gone). In speech, the simple perfeito or imperfeito often replaces it, but you need it for clear sequences.
